hypotheses.construction_plan: Treat K(n) as the common multiplicative kernel. Introduce one slot after K(n); the product members are generated by substituting a(n) or b(n) into the slot, and the bare K(n) member is the neutral specialization slot -> 1.
required_assumptions: K(n) is a nontrivial common subexpression across the three members
The multiplicative identity 1 can serve as a neutral slot value for the bare occurrence, so K(n)*1 normalizes to K(n)
hypotheses.rationale: F01 shows a one-hole product pattern K(n)*theta0 with a(n) and b(n) as instances; F02 reports K(n) itself as the shared CSE subexpression. A single product template with a neutral specialization captures both the product family and the bare kernel occurrence without changing the two observed product expressions.
